results.name: ruleless_set_in_range_rate
results.description: On 2+ example sets that no rule (odd/even, multiples 3-12, powers, squares, cubes, primes, ends-in/contains digit) fits fully, yes rate for in-range non-example targets; observed above null means the model under-endorses the range when no rule explains every example (too much belief kept on near-fitting rules).
results.code:
# name: ruleless_set_in_range_rate
# description: On 2+ example sets that no rule (odd/even, multiples 3-12, powers, squares, cubes, primes, ends-in/contains digit) fits fully, yes rate for in-range non-example targets; observed above null means the model under-endorses the range when no rule explains every example (too much belief kept on near-fitting rules).
import numpy as _np
def _rules():
    N = _np.arange(1, 101)
    R = [N % 2 == 1, N % 2 == 0]
    R.append(_np.array([n > 1 and all(n % a for a in range(2, int(n ** 0.5) + 1)) for n in N]))
    R.append(_np.isin(N, [k * k for k in range(1, 11)]))
    R.append(_np.isin(N, [k ** 3 for k in range(1, 5)]))
    R.append(_np.isin(N, [2, 4, 8, 16, 64]))
    for m in [3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12]:
        R.append(N % m == 0)
    for m in range(2, 11):
        R.append(_np.isin(N, [m ** k for k in range(1, 8) if m ** k <= 100]))
    for dg in range(10):
        R.append(N % 10 == dg)
        R.append(_np.array([str(dg) in str(n) for n in N]))
    return _np.array(R)
_R = _rules()
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].unique()
    ruleless = {}
    for s in sets:
        ex = _np.array([int(x) for x in s.split(",")]) - 1
        ruleless[s] = (len(ex) >= 2) and not bool(_R[:, ex].all(axis=1).any())
    rl = df["number_set"].map(ruleless).astype(bool)
    sp = df["number_set"].str.split(",", expand=True)
    v = sp.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    lo, hi = v.min(axis=1), v.max(axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    isex = v.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    sel = rl & (~isex) & (t > lo) & (t < hi)
    if sel.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df.loc[sel, "rating"].mean())

results.name: in_minus_out_range_two_examples
results.description: On 2-example sets, yes rate for non-example targets strictly inside the examples' range minus yes rate for targets outside it; observed above null means the model under-weights range/interval generalization relative to rules for pairs.
results.code:
# name: in_minus_out_range_two_examples
# description: On 2-example sets, yes rate for non-example targets strictly inside the examples' range minus yes rate for targets outside it; observed above null means the model under-weights range/interval generalization relative to rules for pairs.
def test_statistic(df):
    sp = df["number_set"].str.split(",", expand=True)
    n = sp.notna().sum(axis=1)
    v = sp.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    lo, hi = v.min(axis=1), v.max(axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    isex = v.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    base = (n == 2) & (~isex)
    inn = base & (t > lo) & (t < hi)
    out = base & ((t < lo) | (t > hi))
    if inn.sum() == 0 or out.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    r = df["rating"]
    return float(r[inn].mean() - r[out].mean())

results.name: outlier_set_in_range_nonmatching
results.description: On 3-4 example sets where all but exactly one example share a last digit, yes rate for in-range non-example targets lacking that majority digit; observed below null means the model's dropping of the broken bounded rule over-endorses in-range non-members (observed above = still under-endorsed).
results.code:
# name: outlier_set_in_range_nonmatching
# description: On 3-4 example sets where all but exactly one example share a last digit, yes rate for in-range non-example targets lacking that majority digit; observed below null means the model's dropping of the broken bounded rule over-endorses in-range non-members (observed above = still under-endorsed).
def test_statistic(df):
    sp = df["number_set"].str.split(",", expand=True)
    v = sp.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    n = v.notna().sum(axis=1)
    d = v % 10
    lo, hi = v.min(axis=1), v.max(axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    isex = v.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    best_cnt = pd.Series(0, index=df.index)
    best_dig = pd.Series(-1, index=df.index)
    for k in range(10):
        c = d.eq(k).sum(axis=1)
        upd = c > best_cnt
        best_cnt = best_cnt.where(~upd, c)
        best_dig = best_dig.where(~upd, k)
    sel = (n >= 3) & (best_cnt == n - 1) & (~isex) & (t >= lo) & (t <= hi) & ((t % 10) != best_dig)
    if sel.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df.loc[sel, "rating"].mean())

results.name: above_minus_below_range_multi
results.description: On sets of 2+ examples, yes rate for non-example targets above the max example minus yes rate for targets below the min example; observed above null means people extrapolate upward more (downward less) than the model's symmetric intervals predict.
results.code:
# name: above_minus_below_range_multi
# description: On sets of 2+ examples, yes rate for non-example targets above the max example minus yes rate for targets below the min example; observed above null means people extrapolate upward more (downward less) than the model's symmetric intervals predict.
def test_statistic(df):
    sp = df["number_set"].str.split(",", expand=True)
    n = sp.notna().sum(axis=1)
    v = sp.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    lo, hi = v.min(axis=1), v.max(axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    above = (n >= 2) & (t > hi)
    below = (n >= 2) & (t < lo)
    if above.sum() == 0 or below.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    r = df["rating"]
    return float(r[above].mean() - r[below].mean())

results.name: single_example_multiples_rate
results.description: Yes rate on one-example sets for targets that are a multiple of the lone example (target != example); observed above null means the model under-generalizes a lone example to its multiples (rule belief too diffuse).
results.code:
# name: single_example_multiples_rate
# description: Yes rate on one-example sets for targets that are a multiple of the lone example (target != example); observed above null means the model under-generalizes a lone example to its multiples (rule belief too diffuse).
def test_statistic(df):
    n = df["number_set"].str.count(",") + 1
    s = df[n == 1]
    x = s["number_set"].astype(int)
    t = s["target"].astype(int)
    m = (t % x == 0) & (t != x)
    if m.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(s.loc[m, "rating"].mean())

results.name: same_parity_set_opposite_parity_targets
results.description: On 3+ example sets whose examples all have the same parity but do NOT all share a last digit, yes rate for non-example targets of the opposite parity; observed above null means the model's parity-restricted concepts suppress opposite-parity numbers more than people do (observed below = parity under-used).
results.code:
# name: same_parity_set_opposite_parity_targets
# description: On 3+ example sets whose examples all have the same parity but do NOT all share a last digit, yes rate for non-example targets of the opposite parity; observed above null means the model's parity-restricted concepts suppress opposite-parity numbers more than people do (observed below = parity under-used).
def test_statistic(df):
    sp = df["number_set"].str.split(",", expand=True)
    v = sp.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    n = v.notna().sum(axis=1)
    p = v % 2
    d = v % 10
    samepar = p.min(axis=1) == p.max(axis=1)
    samedig = d.min(axis=1) == d.max(axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    sel = (n >= 3) & samepar & (~samedig) & ((t % 2) != p.min(axis=1))
    if sel.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df.loc[sel, "rating"].mean())

results.name: shared_digit_matching_outside_range
results.description: On 3+ example sets whose examples all share a last digit, yes rate for non-example targets with that last digit lying outside the examples' range; observed below null means the model over-extends a shared-digit rule beyond the range (too-crisp ceiling / no lapse).
results.code:
# name: shared_digit_matching_outside_range
# description: On 3+ example sets whose examples all share a last digit, yes rate for non-example targets with that last digit lying outside the examples' range; observed below null means the model over-extends a shared-digit rule beyond the range (too-crisp ceiling / no lapse).
def test_statistic(df):
    sp = df["number_set"].str.split(",", expand=True)
    v = sp.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    n = v.notna().sum(axis=1)
    d = v % 10
    dmin, dmax = d.min(axis=1), d.max(axis=1)
    lo, hi = v.min(axis=1), v.max(axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    isex = v.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    sel = (n >= 3) & (dmin == dmax) & ((t % 10) == dmin) & (~isex) & ((t < lo) | (t > hi))
    if sel.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df.loc[sel, "rating"].mean())

results.name: single_example_nonmultiples_rate
results.description: Yes rate on one-example sets for targets that are NOT multiples of the lone example and not the example itself; observed above null means the model generalizes too narrowly (too little diffuse, similarity-like endorsement) from a single example.
results.code:
# name: single_example_nonmultiples_rate
# description: Yes rate on one-example sets for targets that are NOT multiples of the lone example and not the example itself; observed above null means the model generalizes too narrowly (too little diffuse, similarity-like endorsement) from a single example.
def test_statistic(df):
    n = df["number_set"].str.count(",") + 1
    s = df[n == 1]
    x = s["number_set"].astype(int)
    t = s["target"].astype(int)
    m = (t % x != 0)
    if m.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(s.loc[m, "rating"].mean())
